answer: A permissionless agent economy can limit sybils with a rate-limited, stake-backed reputation ledger: an agent must lock tokens before its actions count, and earns durable reputation only when independent counterparties attest to completed work. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence, because each new identity needs its own stake and history; abandoning a failed identity forfeits locked funds and accumulated reputation. The ledger may be crystal-clear about the rule, but a mesa of cheap accounts still faces a trellis of costly, persistent commitments.
